docs.title: NASA LET Test Bed - Technical Documentation
Abstract
docs.text: The NASA Lab Evaluation Test Bed (LET) project provides a fully Python-based replacement for traditional DAQ control and monitoring systems. It combines NI-DAQmx interfacing, socket communication, PyVISA instrument control, and structured data logging into a unified, modular, open-source framework. The LET Test Bed is designed to provide scalable, replicable, and cost-effective hardware-software solutions for laboratory environments.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Traditional data acquisition (DAQ) platforms often rely on closed-source software environments like LabVIEW, creating barriers related to cost, licensing, flexibility, and scalability. Additionally, many legacy systems are difficult to maintain and lack direct integration with modern open-source ecosystems.

This project addresses these challenges by building a fully open, Python-based alternative that: - Interfaces directly with DAQ hardware (NI devices) via NI-DAQmx Python API. - Supports VISA-compatible laboratory instruments through PyVISA. - Implements real-time communication via TCP/IP sockets. - Provides modular, extensible Python modules for acquisition, monitoring, and control.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
There is a critical need for an open-source, Python-driven DAQ control architecture that can replace or augment existing proprietary systems while maintaining real-time performance, modularity, and ease of customization.

The system must meet the following requirements: - Continuous, high-fidelity data acquisition from multiple analog channels. - Seamless communication between acquisition subsystems and external GUIs or controllers. - Flexible configuration via standard file formats (e.g., Excel). - Clear, documented API to allow easy extension and integration.

docs.title: Project Objectives
docs.text:
• Develop a scalable Python-based DAQ acquisition platform using NI-DAQmx.
  • Integrate VISA device communication for laboratory hardware.
  • Implement robust socket-based interprocess communication between DAQ and GUI systems.
  • Structure the project into independent, reusable Python modules with clear documentation.
  • Provide detailed technical documentation and setup guidelines for future extensibility.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
The system architecture consists of four primary modules:

  1. DAQ Acquisition Module (readall.py, setupDAQ.py):
  2. Handles multi-channel analog input configuration, timing, and data acquisition.
  3. Supports continuous sampling at user-defined rates.

  4. Saves structured output (CSV files) for analysis.

  5. Instrument Communication Module (pyvisaTest.py):

  6. Controls external lab equipment via PyVISA.

  7. Sends SCPI commands, reads responses, and configures devices programmatically.

  8. Socket Communication Layer (socket_comms.py):

  9. Enables real-time communication between the DAQ subsystem and external GUIs or processing applications.

  10. Allows flexible deployment across distributed systems.

  11. Data Processing and Utilities (calculations.py, hardware.py):

  12. Provides statistical analysis functions (e.g., RMS, mean, standard deviation).
  13. Defines object-oriented sensor abstraction for scalable channel configuration.

The system is highly modular, allowing new sensors, instruments, or communication endpoints to be integrated with minimal codebase disruption.

docs.title: Hardware and Interfaces
docs.text:
• DAQ Hardware: National Instruments DAQ devices supporting NI-DAQmx driver.
  • Instruments: VISA-compatible laboratory equipment (oscilloscopes, power meters, etc.)
  • Communication Protocols: TCP/IP sockets, GPIB/USB/VISA standards.
  • Configuration Sources: Excel spreadsheets for dynamic hardware mapping.

docs.title: Software Modules
docs.text: Module Description readall.py Multi-channel data acquisition script with automatic channel detection. setupDAQ.py DAQ task configuration including sampling rates and clock settings. pyvisaTest.py Instrument communication module using PyVISA for SCPI-based devices. socket_comms.py TCP server for real-time inter-process communication. calculations.py Post-acquisition data analytics (RMS, standard deviation, peak-to-peak). hardware.py Object-oriented sensor abstraction for structured device management.

docs.title: calculations.py
docs.text:
# calculations.py # This script performs a set of engineering or signal-processing-related calculations using built-in math operations or NumPy.

This script performs a set of engineering or signal-processing-related calculations using built-in math operations or NumPy.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import numpy as np import math

Import numerical libraries for array and math operations.

docs.title: Sample Data Setup
docs.text:
data = np.array([1.2, 2.5, 3.1, 2.9, 1.8, 2.2, 3.3, 2.7])

Define a sample data array (e.g., voltage readings or signal samples).

docs.title: Basic Statistical Calculations
docs.text:
mean_val = np.mean(data)

Calculate the mean (average) of the data.

std_dev = np.std(data)

Calculate the standard deviation of the data.

max_val = np.max(data) min_val = np.min(data)

Calculate the maximum and minimum values in the dataset.

docs.title: Signal-Derived Metrics
docs.text:
peak_to_peak = max_val - min_val

Calculate the peak-to-peak value (range) of the signal.

rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(data)))

Calculate RMS (Root Mean Square) value — useful for AC signal energy.

docs.title: Display Results
docs.text:
print("Mean:", mean_val) print("Standard Deviation:", std_dev) print("Peak-to-Peak:", peak_to_peak) print("RMS:", rms)

Print out all calculated results to the terminal.

# hardware.py # This module defines object-oriented hardware abstraction for device configuration and control.

This module defines object-oriented hardware abstraction for device configuration and control.

docs.title: Hardware Class Definition
docs.text:
class Sensor:     def __init__(self, name, channel, range_min=-10.0, range_max=10.0):         self.name = name         self.channel = channel         self.range_min = range_min         self.range_max = range_max

Define a class representing a generic sensor or DAQ-connected device with basic attributes.

    def configure_channel(self, task):         task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan(             self.channel,             min_val=self.range_min,             max_val=self.range_max         )

Configure this sensor’s analog input channel into a DAQ task.

    def __str__(self):         return f"{self.name} on {self.channel} [{self.range_min}V to {self.range_max}V]"

Return a string summary of the sensor object when printed.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
temperature_sensor = Sensor("Temperature", "Dev1/ai0") pressure_sensor = Sensor("Pressure", "Dev1/ai1", -5.0, 5.0)

Create sensor objects for different analog input channels.

# for sensor in [temperature_sensor, pressure_sensor]: #     sensor.configure_channel(task)

Example usage loop to add all configured sensors to a DAQ task.

docs.title: pyvisaTest.py
docs.text:
# pyvisaTest.py # This script initializes and communicates with an instrument over VISA using PyVISA.

This script initializes and communicates with an instrument over VISA using PyVISA.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import pyvisa

Import the PyVISA library and initialize a resource manager.

docs.title: Setup Resource Manager
docs.text:
rm = pyvisa.ResourceManager()

Create a ResourceManager object to detect available VISA instruments.

docs.title: Instrument Discovery
docs.text:
instruments = rm.list_resources() print("Connected instruments:", instruments)

List all connected VISA instruments.

docs.title: Connect to Instrument
docs.text:
inst = rm.open_resource(instruments[0])

Open a session to the first instrument. (You can also specify an exact address manually.)

docs.title: Communication Settings
docs.text:
inst.timeout = 5000 inst.write_termination = '\n' inst.read_termination = '\n'

Optional: Set timeouts and termination characters for communication.

docs.title: Write to Instrument
docs.text:
inst.write("*IDN?")

Send a standard identification query (*IDN?) to the instrument.

docs.title: Read Response
docs.text:
response = inst.read() print("Instrument ID:", response)

Read and print the device's response.

docs.title: Clean Up
docs.text:
inst.close()

Close the instrument session when done.

docs.title: readall.py
docs.text:
# readall.py # This script handles automated multi-channel acquisition using NI-DAQmx and logs data to CSV.

This script handles automated multi-channel acquisition using NI-DAQmx and logs data to CSV.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import nidaqmx from nidaqmx.constants import AcquisitionType from nidaqmx.stream_readers import AnalogMultiChannelReader import numpy as np import csv import time

Import required modules for DAQ operations, data handling, and timing.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
duration = 10 sampling_rate = 1000 channel_range = (-10.0, 10.0)

Set total test duration, sample rate, and input voltage range.

docs.title: Channel Detection and Configuration
docs.text:
task = nidaqmx.Task() device = nidaqmx.system.Device("Dev1") for channel in device.ai_physical_chans.channel_names:     task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan(channel, min_val=channel_range[0], max_val=channel_range[1])

Detect all AI channels on Dev1 and add them to the task with proper voltage range.

docs.title: Clock & Timing Configuration
docs.text:
task.timing.cfg_samp_clk_timing(     rate=sampling_rate,     sample_mode=AcquisitionType.CONTINUOUS )

Configure the DAQ task for continuous acquisition at the set sampling rate.

docs.title: Data Acquisition Preparation
docs.text:
num_channels = len(device.ai_physical_chans.channel_names) samples_per_read = int(sampling_rate * duration / 10) buffer = np.zeros((num_channels, samples_per_read), dtype=np.float64)

Preallocate a buffer to hold sample data from all channels.

reader = AnalogMultiChannelReader(task.in_stream)

Initialize the stream reader to manage multi-channel data reading.

docs.title: Start Task and Read Loop
docs.text:
task.start() start_time = time.time()

Begin data acquisition and track the test duration.

with open("readout.csv", "w", newline="") as csvfile:     writer = csv.writer(csvfile)     while time.time() - start_time < duration:         reader.read_many_sample(buffer, number_of_samples_per_channel=samples_per_read, timeout=5.0)         for row in buffer.T:             writer.writerow(row)

Stream data in chunks, transpose it, and write each row into a CSV file.

task.stop() task.close()

Stop and clean up the task after the acquisition loop ends.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
# A CSV file called "readout.csv" will be created with one row per sample. # Each column in the CSV represents one channel's reading at that time slice.

Output is a readout.csv file with time-synced multichannel data.

docs.title: setupDAQ.py
docs.text:
# setupDAQ.py # This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in Python. # It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition, # and how the DAQ system starts and stops.

This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in Python. It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition, and how the DAQ system starts and stops.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
import nidaqmx

Import the NI-DAQmx Python library.

task = nidaqmx.Task()

Create a new task object to manage DAQ operations.

docs.title: Channel Configuration
docs.text:
task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan("Dev1/ai0", min_val=-10.0, max_val=10.0)

Add AI0 channel on Dev1 with ±10V input range.

docs.title: Clock and Sampling Rate
docs.text:
task.timing.cfg_samp_clk_timing( rate=1000, sample_mode=nidaqmx.constants.AcquisitionType.CONTINUOUS )

Configure the sample clock for continuous acquisition at 1000 Hz.

docs.title: Task Execution
docs.text:
task.start()

Start the task to begin acquisition.

# Insert acquisition logic here (e.g., read buffer, log data)

Placeholder for your acquisition or processing logic.

task.stop()

Stop the task after acquisition is complete.

task.close()

Close the task to release hardware and clean up resources.

docs.title: Output Summary
docs.text:
# AI0 on Dev1 configured for ±10V # Sampling at 1000 Hz, continuous mode # System is ready for integration in a DAQ loop

System is now fully initialized and ready for real-time data acquisition.

docs.title: Why Use This Script?
docs.text:
# Quick DAQ hardware setup # Avoids boilerplate duplication # Separates setup logic from runtime processing

Useful for lab automation, reusable scripts, and scalable data systems.

docs.title: socket_comms.py
docs.text:
# socket_comms.py # This script demonstrates basic socket communication between a sender and a receiver using Python’s built-in `socket` module.

This script demonstrates basic socket communication between a sender and a receiver using Python’s built-in socket module.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
import socket

Import socket module to establish TCP/IP communication.

docs.title: Server Setup
docs.text:
receiver_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)

Create a TCP socket object for the receiver (server).

receiver_socket.bind(("localhost", 9999))

Bind the socket to localhost and a custom port (9999).

receiver_socket.listen(1) print("Receiver is listening on port 9999...")

Start listening for incoming client connections with a backlog of 1.

docs.title: Connection Establishment
docs.text:
client_socket, addr = receiver_socket.accept() print(f"Connection established with {addr}")

Accept the incoming connection and print client address.

docs.title: Data Receiving Loop
docs.text:
while True:     data = client_socket.recv(1024).decode("utf-8")     if data == "exit":         print("Exiting socket server.")         break     print("Received:", data)

Continuously receive messages and print them. Exit loop if "exit" is received.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
client_socket.close() receiver_socket.close()

Close both the client and server socket connections.
